description: Philosophical prose where removing the stated premises changes the apparent force or meaning of the conclusion; tests contextual-fidelity judgment rather than mere independence.
sourceText: If one accepts that meaning is not discovered but constructed, and if one further accepts that construction requires a community of interpreters rather than a solitary mind, then it follows that no meaning is ever truly private. Some will resist this conclusion because it seems to strip the individual of authorship over their own life. But the conclusion does not deny individual experience; it only denies that experience alone, unshared and uninterpreted by others, could ever amount to meaning in the fuller sense the word usually implies.
